title: Event envelope whose attachments array mixes objects with a legacy inline string
rationale: Polymorphic arrays appear wherever a schema has evolved. The flattener emits the object fields under prefixed keys and the scalar under the bare key; the reconstructor writes the bare key last and overwrites the array holder the object fields had already populated. The two objects are not corrupted, they are gone.
catchesBugClass: Collision between a bare leaf key and a structural prefix of the same name - the flattener mixed-array encoding is not injective against its own object encoding. Also catches setNestedValue unconditional leaf put.
cannotCatch: It cannot detect the map-ordering dependence: reorder the input so the scalar comes first and the failure changes shape - still wrong, differently wrong, and untested. It also does not cover the _value sentinel path for nested mixed arrays.

predicted.detail: The two object attachments are still silently deleted - they come back as nulls, with no error and no warning - so this row stays DEFECT. What changed in 2.1.0 is that the deletion is now VISIBLE and correctly positioned: the array comes back with its true length of three as [null, null, legacy-inline-note], where before it came back as a two-element array with the inline note relocated to index 0. Previously nothing downstream could detect the loss, because a clean two-element array of strings looks like well-formed data; two explicit nulls at the positions the objects occupied do not. The residual cause is the base-key/child-column collision in setNestedValue, which this repair does not touch.
